title: Mandawa: The Open-Air Art Gallery of Rajasthan
content:
Mandawa

Mandawa, a small town in the Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan, is often called the “Open-Air Art Gallery” of India. Famous for its beautiful havelis, grand forts, and stunning fresco paintings, Mandawa is a hidden gem in the Shekhawati region that attracts history lovers, art enthusiasts, and travelers from around the world.

History of Mandawa

Mandawa was founded in the 18th century by the Rajput rulers and became a popular settlement for wealthy merchants. These merchants built lavish havelis (mansions) with intricately painted walls and decorated courtyards to showcase their prosperity. Even today, these havelis stand as a testimony to Rajasthan’s rich cultural and artistic heritage.

Top Attractions in Mandawa

1. Mandawa Fort

Built in the 18th century, Mandawa Fort is the pride of the town. With its impressive architecture, painted archways, and royal interiors, the fort gives visitors a glimpse into the grandeur of Rajasthan’s royal past. Today, it has been converted into a heritage hotel, offering tourists a royal stay experience.

Famous Havelis of Mandawa

Mandawa is known for its ornate havelis, decorated with vibrant frescoes and mirror work. Some of the most famous ones include:

  • Jhunjhunwala Haveli - Known for its grand entrance and stunning wall paintings.
  • Murmuria Haveli - Famous for its frescoes depicting cars, trains, and even European figures.
  • Gulab Rai Ladia Haveli - Admired for its detailed paintings and intricate architecture.

Frescoes and Wall Paintings

The frescoes in Mandawa are the town’s main highlight. They depict mythological stories, daily life, historical events, and even modern inventions of the time. Walking through Mandawa feels like walking in an art museum under the open sky.

Things to Do in Mandawa

  • Explore the narrow lanes filled with heritage charm.
  • Visit the colorful bazaars to shop for handicrafts, textiles, and traditional jewelry.
  • Enjoy a heritage stay at Mandawa Fort or other restored havelis.
  • Capture the stunning frescoes and architecture through photography.

Best Time to Visit Mandawa

The best time to visit Mandawa is during the winter months (October to March) when the weather is pleasant for sightseeing and exploring the heritage sites.

Timings & Entry Fees

  • Mandawa Fort: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Entry fee around ₹100 - ₹200
  • Havelis: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Entry fees may vary from ₹50 - ₹100 per haveli

How to Reach Mandawa

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Jaipur (around 170 km away).
  • By Train: Jhunjhunu Railway Station is the closest (around 30 km).
  • By Road: Mandawa is well-connected by road to major cities like Jaipur, Delhi, and Bikaner.
